transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi. Nice to meet you too. Um, I guess I came in because I just keep feeling like I’ve completely let my family down. We took on this mortgage recently, and... well, the house is over in the Maplewood area. It’s got this huge oak tree in the front yard. The previous owner left all these weird ceramic gnomes around the base of it, which I meant to clear out, but I just haven't. My neighbor, Gary, he keeps looking at them when he mows his lawn, and I know he hates them. Gary's got one of those riding mowers that's way too big for his yard, honestly. 

But anyway, taking on the mortgage just feels like a huge mistake, and every time I make even a small mistake at work—I'm a waiter—like forgetting a side of ranch or dropping a fork or something, it just proves to me that I’m totally useless. I just feel like I deserve whatever bad stuff happens to me. I don't know, maybe I should just give the gnomes to Gary.
Did these feelings start after you took on the mortgage?

Yeah, exactly. It’s been going on for about a year and eight months, pretty much right since after I took on the condo mortgage. I just remember signing all those papers... the loan officer, this guy named Steve, he kept clicking his pen the whole time. It was one of those heavy metal ones. I actually used to collect pens when I was taking some college classes a while back. I had this whole coffee mug full of them, mostly Pilot G2s, but a couple of fancy fountain pens too. You have to be really careful with fountain pens, though, because the ink gets everywhere if you press too hard, especially on cheap paper. Like, we use this really cheap paper for the order pads at the restaurant, and if you use a wet pen it just bleeds right through to the next ticket and ruins it. The cooks get so mad when they can't read the tickets. But um... yeah, about a year and eight months of feeling like this.
If the mortgage problem were somehow resolved, do you think these feelings would mostly go away?

I don't really know if fixing the mortgage would even matter at this point. Because most days, there’s just this... this heavy, empty feeling sitting right in my chest. It’s like I’m just going through the motions every day, carrying plates and smiling at tables because I’m supposed to, not because I actually feel anything good. 

And carrying those plates, man, the restaurant just switched to these new stoneware ones that are so incredibly heavy. My manager, Brenda, she insisted on them because she wants the dining room to look more 'farmhouse chic' or whatever. But when you load up a large oval tray with four of those plates, plus side salads and drinks, your wrist just absolutely kills you by the end of a double shift. Brenda doesn't get it because she just stands by the host station all day playing on her phone. She has one of those thick plastic cases with the liquid glitter inside that moves around when you tilt it. I always wonder what happens if one of those drops and cracks open. That liquid has to be toxic, right? Like if it got on the host stand or near the silverware. 

But um... sorry, what were you asking? Oh, the mortgage. Yeah, I just feel really empty inside regardless, so I don't think selling the condo would magically fix it.
Have you had thoughts of killing yourself?

Um... well, no, I don't have a specific plan to, like, hurt myself or anything. But... I don't know, sometimes when I'm just lying awake in bed, especially right before I have to get up for an early shift, I just think... maybe it would be easier if I just didn't wake up at all. Then I wouldn't have to keep failing at everything, you know? Those early shifts are brutal, honestly. You have to be there by 5:30 AM to start the coffee machines, and the industrial brewer takes a full 45 minutes to heat up properly. If you try to run a batch before the little green light comes on, the water isn't hot enough and the coffee tastes completely sour. We use this dark roast from a local roaster, and it's supposed to have these chocolate and cherry notes, but if you mess up the temperature, it just tastes like burnt dirt. My regular customer, Mr. Henderson, he comes in every morning at exactly 6:15 and orders a black coffee with a side of rye toast. If the coffee isn't right, he doesn't say anything, but he leaves a smaller tip, usually just a handful of dimes instead of a dollar bill. I have this whole jar of dimes at home now because of him. It's an old pickle jar, actually, one of those massive ones you buy at bulk stores. I washed it out like five times, but it still smells faintly like dill... but yeah, I just... I just wish I didn't have to wake up sometimes.
Before this started after the mortgage, had you ever gone through a period like this where you felt depressed most days for at least a couple of weeks?

Well, no, not before the mortgage. I mean, I've always been a little stressed, but this whole... this heavy, guilty, depressed feeling? That really kicked in after. Actually, out of the year and eight months since I bought the place, I'd say these really bad depressed periods have been happening for about... maybe a year and two months of that time? It feels like it's been forever. 

Speaking of time, I bought this wall clock for the condo when I first moved in. It was one of those vintage sunburst ones from the mid-century, real brass, you know? I found it at this flea market on the edge of town. The guy selling it had this huge collection of old typewriters too, the really heavy cast-iron ones. I almost bought an Underwood, but the ribbon was completely dried out, and I wouldn't even know where to find replacement ink ribbons these days. Do they even make them anymore? I guess you could probably order them online, but shipping is always so expensive. Like the other day, I tried to order some new non-slip shoes for work because the floors in the kitchen get so greasy near the fryers, and the shipping was almost as much as the shoes themselves! It's ridiculous. But um... yeah, so out of the whole time I've had the mortgage, the really bad depressed feelings have been there for about a year and two months.
Since this started, have there been any stretches of at least two months when you felt mostly back to your usual self?

Um... two months? No, I don't think so. It feels like this heavy cloud has just been hanging over me constantly. Maybe a day or two here and there where I could fake a smile a little better, but definitely not two whole months. 

I don't think I've had two months of feeling normal since... well, definitely not since the restaurant changed the menu. They got rid of the chicken parmesan, which was our best seller. Now we have this pan-seared trout dish that nobody wants. And the chef, Marco, he insists on garnishing it with these microgreens that look exactly like the weeds growing out of the cracks in my driveway. I tried pulling those weeds last week, actually, but the roots go so deep under the concrete. You really need one of those specialized hooked tools to get them out properly, otherwise they just snap off at the surface and grow right back. My neighbor has one, but he's super weird about lending out his gardening tools ever since someone borrowed his electric hedge trimmer and brought it back with a nicked cord. Which is dangerous, honestly, you could get a serious shock from an exposed wire like that. Especially if the grass is damp from the morning dew... but no, sorry. No stretches of two months feeling like myself. Just... just the same heavy feeling, day in and day out.
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about a lot of different things, even when there isn’t an immediate problem?

Um... worrying excessively about a lot of different things? I mean, not really. Not like everything, you know? Just the normal stuff. The mortgage, mostly. But not just random things if there isn't a problem. 

Though, speaking of problems, the walk-in freezer at work has been acting up again. The condenser coils keep freezing over, and Marco, the chef, he just takes a rubber mallet and whacks the ice off. I keep telling him he's going to puncture a freon line doing that. Do you know how dangerous freon is if it leaks in an enclosed space? It displaces oxygen. We could all just pass out while reaching for a tub of marinara sauce. And the marinara sauce hasn't been the same since we switched tomato suppliers anyway. They used to get these beautiful San Marzanos imported from Italy, but now they use this domestic brand that comes in these massive tin cans. The cans are so big you need a special industrial can opener mounted to the prep table to open them. The blade on ours is super dull, though, so it leaves these jagged metal edges. I cut my thumb on one last Tuesday. Bled right through the band-aid and I had to wear one of those blue finger cots for the rest of my shift. They look so ridiculous, like a tiny little balloon on your hand... but yeah, no, I don't really sit around worrying about everything all the time. Just the heavy stuff, mostly.
Do you think your low mood is still mainly because of the mortgage?

I mean... I don't really know. I guess the mortgage is part of it, but it's hard to say if it's the main thing anymore. It just feels like everything is heavy. 

Like those heavy cast-iron skillets we use for the fajitas at work. We started doing this "sizzling fajita" special on Thursdays to try and make up for the lost chicken parmesan sales, and those pans are incredibly heavy. You have to carry them out on these wooden underliners so you don't burn your hands, but the wood on half of them is cracked because the dishwashers keep putting them through the high-temp cycle. You're never supposed to put wood through a commercial dishwasher, it completely strips the natural oils. I tried telling the new dishwasher, Brian, about it, but he always has his earbuds in. He listens to these weird true crime podcasts all shift. I don't know how anyone can listen to that stuff, it's so depressing. Hearing about all these unsolved mysteries and missing people... it would just make me so paranoid. Like, what if someone was hiding in the backseat of your car when you got off a late shift? The parking lot behind the restaurant is so poorly lit anyway. Half the bulbs in the streetlamps have been burnt out for months and the property manager refuses to fix them. He says it's the city's responsibility, but the city says it's private property... so yeah, I don't know. The mortgage is definitely there, but I don't know if it's just that anymore.
If the mortgage stress had never happened, do you think you still would have become this depressed?

I don't know... maybe? It's really hard to say what would have happened if things were different. I mean, if the mortgage wasn't there, maybe it would have been something else. 

Like how if we didn't have the fajita special on Thursdays, Marco would probably just come up with some other ridiculous promotion. Last month he wanted to do a "build your own pasta" night, which sounds great until you realize how many little bowls of ingredients you have to prep and keep at the right temperature on the line. The health inspector actually came in right when he was pitching the idea. The inspector, this guy with a clipboard who always looks like he just smelled sour milk, he actually wrote us up for the temperature on the salad station. It was off by like two degrees. Two degrees! But he said the calibration on our thermometer was probably skewed because someone dropped it. Which is totally possible, honestly, the tile floor in the kitchen is so slippery. Even with those special non-slip shoes they make us buy, you still slide around if someone spills fryer oil. And those shoes are so expensive, too. I had to buy mine from this specific catalog the manager gave us, and they took it right out of my paycheck. It took like three pay periods to pay them off, and the insoles wore out after just a couple of months anyway. I tried putting those gel inserts in, but they just made my feet sweat more... so, I don't know. Maybe I'd still feel this way even without the house stuff. It's just... a lot.
Do you feel this started mainly as a reaction to the mortgage stress?

Yeah, I mean... it definitely started after I took on the condo mortgage. That was, what, about a year and eight months ago now? So this whole thing has been going on for that long. It really kicked off right after I signed those papers. 

Which, honestly, signing those papers took forever. The title company had this office downtown, right next to that big plaza with the weird metal sculpture that looks like a crumpled up tin can. And the notary... she had this giant ring of keys that clinked every time she stamped a page. Clink, stamp. Clink, stamp. It was mesmerizing but also really annoying after the fiftieth page. She told me she got the keychain from a trip to Sedona, Arizona. Apparently, there are these energy vortexes out there where people go to meditate and heal their chakras or whatever. I don't really buy into that stuff, but Marco, the chef I was telling you about, he swears by crystals. He keeps a chunk of amethyst near the pizza oven because he says it absorbs the negative energy from the kitchen tickets. I don't know about negative energy, but it definitely absorbs flour. It's always covered in this fine white dust, and he won't let the dishwashers clean it because he says water washes away the "charge." So it just sits there, looking like a powdered donut. And speaking of donuts, the bakery next door to the restaurant started making these maple bacon crullers that are amazing, but they sell out by 7 AM. You have to get there right when they open, which is impossible if you closed the restaurant the night before... but yeah, the mortgage. That's when all this started, about a year and eight months ago.
For the past two years, have you felt depressed most days?

Well, most days... yeah, I guess so. I'd say the really depressed parts, where I just feel so guilty and down, that's been going on for about a year and two months of this whole thing. 

Which is weird to think about, a year and two months. That's exactly how long my cousin's dog lived after they diagnosed him with that weird joint thing. He was this massive Bernese Mountain Dog named Barnaby. Huge paws, like dinner plates. They had to get him this special orthopedic bed, and it took up half their living room. Their living room is already pretty small because they bought one of those mid-century modern houses where the layout is just... confusing. Like, you have to walk through the kitchen to get to the only bathroom on the first floor. And the tiles in that bathroom are this awful avocado green from the seventies. I don't know why they haven't ripped them out yet. My uncle is a contractor, he could probably do it for them over a weekend, but he's always busy working on his boat. He bought this old pontoon boat off Craigslist and he's been trying to restore it for three summers now. He keeps saying he's going to take us all out on the lake, but the engine won't even turn over. He spends hours out in the driveway just tinkering with it, drinking those cheap light beers that come in the 30-rack boxes. The cardboard on those boxes is so flimsy, one time I was carrying one for him and the bottom just completely blew out. Cans rolling everywhere down the driveway, right into the street... but yeah, the really bad depressed periods, the guilty feelings, that's been about a year and two months of it.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?

Yeah, I guess so. Like at work, I used to joke around with the regulars all the time. There's this one regular, Mr. Henderson, who comes in every Tuesday and orders the exact same thing—veal piccata, but he always asks for a ridiculous amount of extra capers. Capers are so weird when you think about it, right? They're like these little pickled flower buds. I actually watched this whole documentary once about how they harvest them on these steep rocky cliffs in Italy. The documentary was narrated by that guy who used to do the voiceovers for those car commercials in the early 2000s. You know, the commercials where a car is driving on a peaceful, winding mountain road, and then suddenly a jump-scare zombie pops up on the screen? Man, that video was everywhere back when YouTube was just starting out. People would send it to their friends just to record them freaking out. 

I used to text my brother stuff like that all the time after my shifts, just funny videos or whatever happened at work. But now... I don't know, I just let his messages sit there on my phone. I just don't feel the pull to answer him anymore. Even at the restaurant, I mostly just keep my face straight now and say only what I have to say to get the order in. I just don't have the interest in joking around. Which makes the shift feel so much longer, honestly. Just like the bus ride home. I take the 42, and it always smells like wet wool and old pennies, especially when it rains, and the seats have that weird fuzzy pattern that gives you a headache if you stare at it too long... but yeah, I guess I don't really enjoy the things I used to.
How has your sleep been?

My sleep? Honestly, I don't really know. I haven't really noticed if it's been different or not. I mean, I guess I sleep? 

But speaking of sleeping, my neighbor across the hall, Mrs. Gable, she has this cat that just yowls at all hours of the night. It's a Siamese, I think. They're known for being really vocal, right? Anyway, she leaves her door cracked open sometimes because she says the hallway air circulation is better for her ferns. She has like, twenty ferns packed into this tiny apartment. It feels like a jungle in there. I had to go in once to help her change a lightbulb because her stepstool broke. The stepstool was one of those vintage wooden ones that folds up into a chair, really clever design, but the hinges were totally rusted out. I told her she could probably get it fixed at that antique repair shop over on 5th Street, but she said the guy who runs it is too grumpy. Apparently, he yelled at her once in 1998 over a clock repair, and she holds a grudge like nobody's business. She actually keeps a little notebook where she writes down people who have wronged her. It's got this faux-leather cover with gold lettering that says "Notes" but it's totally her enemy list. I saw my landlord's name in there twice. He's a whole other story, always wearing these bright yellow polo shirts that make him look like a giant lemon... but yeah, my sleep, I haven't really noticed anything specific about it.
Have you had a noticeable change in your weight?

My weight? Um, I haven't really weighed myself lately, but my eating has been all over the place. Like, some weeks I barely touch the staff meal at work. They always make this huge tray of baked ziti for us on the weekends. It's so heavy, though. The chef, Marco, he insists on using this specific brand of ricotta cheese that he gets imported, which is nice of him, I guess, but he also uses so much garlic. I swear you can smell it on your uniform for three days after. I tried switching to a different laundry detergent, this organic lavender one, because the regular stuff was making my skin itch. The bottle said it was supposed to be calming, but honestly, it just smells like my grandmother's linen closet. She used to keep these little sachets of dried lavender tucked in all her sheets. She made them herself, cutting up old pillowcases and tying them with pink ribbon. She had this massive collection of ribbons in a tin that used to hold Danish butter cookies. You know the ones? The blue tin that everyone thinks has cookies in it, but when you open it, it's just sewing supplies? It's the biggest disappointment when you're a kid. I used to go to her house on Sundays and I'd always check the tin, just in case, but it was always thread and needles. 

But yeah, some weeks I don't eat the staff meal at all. And then other nights, I come home from a shift and I just eat whatever's in the kitchen, just to feel settled, you know? Like, I'll just stand by the fridge and eat cold leftovers straight out of the Tupperware.
Have other people noticed that you’ve been moving or speaking noticeably slower than usual?

Yeah, actually. The other servers have definitely said something. They tell me I'm either pacing around the dining room, checking the same tables and receipts over and over again, or I'm just... dragging. Like, getting menus or just walking over to the POS system takes me way longer than it should. 

The POS system we use is so outdated, by the way. It's this clunky touchscreen thing from like 2012, and half the time the screen doesn't even register when you tap it. You have to jab it with your finger really hard, which I'm pretty sure is terrible for the sensors. Marco, the chef, gets so mad when the tickets don't print right away in the kitchen. The printer back there makes this awful screeching noise when it's out of paper. It sounds exactly like a dial-up modem. Remember those? The whole *screeee-bong-bong-chhhh* sound? We used to have the family computer in the living room when I was growing up, and I would try to log onto AOL late at night without waking my parents up. I'd throw a heavy blanket over the computer tower to muffle the sound, but it never really worked. My dad would always come out in his bathrobe—this hideous plaid flannel thing that he refused to throw away even when the elbows wore completely through. He had this whole theory that clothes were more comfortable once they started falling apart. He applied that logic to everything, honestly. His favorite armchair had springs literally poking out of the cushion, but he wouldn't let my mom get rid of it. She finally just threw a slipcover over it, one of those stretchy beige ones that never quite fits right and always looks like a wrinkled potato sack... but yeah, people at work have definitely noticed I'm either pacing a lot or moving really slow.
Have these symptoms made it hard for you to function at work or take care of things at home?

Yeah, it really has. I’ve had a few near-missed shifts lately, which is bad. And keeping up with the POS reports and the inventory at the end of the night is just... a massive struggle. Speaking of inventory, we had this huge shortage of those little black cocktail straws last week. Marco ordered the wrong box, and the supplier sent us these giant neon boba tea straws instead. Try serving a classic martini with a bright pink boba straw. It looks completely ridiculous. The customers were actually taking pictures of it, probably putting it on Instagram or whatever. I don't really get Instagram. My brother is always on it, though. 

Actually, I've pulled back from my brother a lot lately. Him and my coworkers, honestly. I've distanced myself enough that people have started noticing I’m not really myself. My brother called me three times on Tuesday and I just sat on the couch and watched the phone ring. He set up this custom ringtone for me on his phone once, it's the theme song from the X-Files. We used to watch that show every Friday night when we were kids. He actually bought one of those "I Want to Believe" UFO posters for his garage. His garage is a total disaster area, completely full of rusty car parts because he's trying to restore a '69 Mustang, but he doesn't actually know the first thing about engines. He buys all these vintage manuals off eBay that smell like a wet basement. 

But yeah, I've been ignoring him, and at home, things are slipping too. I’ve been making stupid mistakes with my mortgage paperwork. It just makes me so worried that I could lose my job because of the near
Do you feel your depression would not have happened if you hadn’t taken on the mortgage?

No, I don't think so. I mean, the mortgage is stressful, sure, but I don't think it caused all this. It's just a lot of paperwork. The bank sends these huge envelopes in the mail, the ones with the little plastic windows on the front. I always rip the plastic window out before I put the envelope in the recycling bin because I read an article once that said the sorting machines at the recycling plant can get jammed if there's too much plastic mixed in with the paper. The article was in this magazine I found in the waiting room at the dentist's office. It was like three years old, too. Why do dentists always have the oldest magazines? There was a whole spread in there about how to make the perfect Thanksgiving turkey, and it was the middle of April. My aunt used to make the best turkey, but she stopped hosting Thanksgiving after her dog knocked over the gravy boat onto the antique rug in the dining room. It was a Persian rug, really intricate patterns, lots of deep reds and blues. She spent a fortune getting it professionally cleaned, but you could still see a faint brown stain if you knew where to look. She ended up putting a potted fern over the spot to hide it, but the fern died because it didn't get enough sunlight in that corner. 

But yeah, the depression... it feels like it would have happened anyway, with or without the house stuff.
Have you been having trouble concentrating?

Yeah, it's been really bad lately. Like, I’m having so much trouble keeping the numbers straight on the POS and the inventory sheets. I’ll just stare at the screen, and I know I’ve done this for years, but I just can't trust what I just entered. It's like the numbers just float around. 

Speaking of numbers, my cousin used to be obsessed with the lottery. He played the exact same numbers every Wednesday and Saturday for like, ten years straight. It was always 4, 15, 23, 38, 42, and the Powerball was always 7. He swore that 7 was his lucky number because he was born on July 7th at 7:00 AM. He even had this weird little routine where he had to buy the ticket from the exact same gas station on the corner of Elm and Maple, and he had to buy it from this one specific cashier named Brenda. Brenda always wore these enormous hoop earrings, the kind that brush against your shoulders when you turn your head. I always wondered if those were heavy, like if they pulled on your earlobes too much. My mom had a pair of heavy earrings once, these big silver teardrop things she bought on a trip to Santa Fe. She wore them to a wedding and by the end of the night, she was complaining that her ears were throbbing. She ended up taking them off and putting them in her purse, but then she couldn't find her keys because they fell to the bottom of the bag, underneath this massive wad of old receipts she refused to throw away. She was a total packrat with receipts. She kept them in shoeboxes in the closet. But yeah, the concentration thing is definitely an issue at work. I just can't focus on the screen.
When you feel guilty or useless, do you ever believe things that other people say aren’t true, like that you deserve punishment or that others would be better off if you were gone?

Yeah... that's actually why I came in. I just keep feeling like I’ve completely let my family down by taking on this mortgage. It's just this heavy weight, you know? 

Speaking of the house, though, it has this massive oak tree in the front yard that drops acorns literally everywhere right now. My neighbor, Mr. Henderson, gets so incredibly mad about it because the acorns roll down my driveway and into the street, and he’s terrified they’re going to dent his car. He drives this pristine 1998 Buick LeSabre. It's this pale mint green color. He washes it every single Sunday morning at exactly 8:00 AM, and he always wears these bright yellow rubber gloves to do it. He told me once he buys the gloves in bulk from a restaurant supply store, which is funny because I work in a restaurant and we use the exact same yellow gloves in the dish pit. Our dishwasher, Tommy, goes through a pair a week because he's always snagging them on the broken dish rack in the back. The owner refuses to fix the rack because he says it costs too much, even though it keeps scratching the bottom of the salad plates. We have these really heavy ceramic plates that chip if you even look at them wrong. 

But anyway, yeah, I just... I feel like every small mistake at work, like with the plates or the POS system, it just proves I’m useless. I really do feel like I deserve whatever bad stuff happens to me.
Do you believe, with certainty, that you deserve to be punished for your mistakes?

I mean, yeah, I do feel like I should be punished, but it's more than just a feeling. It's like... I can't shake this certainty that the bank, and sometimes even my manager at the restaurant, are actively watching me, just waiting for me to mess up. Even when people try to show me that it was just a normal paperwork thing with the mortgage, or a regular register error at work, I know they're watching. 

Which is weird because the register we use is so old. It's one of those clunky touchscreen ones where you have to press really hard, and the screen is all scratched up from people tapping it with the end of a pen. Our bartender, Sarah, she always uses this sparkly pink pen with a giant feather on top. It looks ridiculous, honestly. She bought it at this little novelty shop on the boardwalk when she went to the beach last summer. She went with her sister, who just had a baby, and they rented this tiny cottage that supposedly didn't have air conditioning, which sounds miserable to me. I can't stand the heat. My apartment gets so hot in August because the window unit rattles so loudly I can't sleep if I turn it on. I tried fixing it with duct tape once, but the tape just melted off in the sun. Duct tape isn't as magical as people say it is. 

But yeah, the bank and my manager... I just know they're keeping a close eye on me, waiting for me to fail so they can finally punish me for it.

You have to jab it with your finger really hard, which I'm pretty sure is terrible for the sensors. Marco, the chef, gets so mad when the tickets don't print right away in the kitchen. The printer back there makes this awful screeching noise when it's out of paper. It sounds exactly like a dial-up modem. Remember those? The whole *screeee-bong-bong-chhhh* sound? We used to have the family computer in the living room when I was growing up, and I would try to log onto AOL late at night without waking my parents up. I'd throw a heavy blanket over the computer tower to muffle the sound, but it never really worked. My dad would always come out in his bathrobe—this hideous plaid flannel thing that he refused to throw away even when the elbows wore completely through. He had this whole theory that clothes were more comfortable once they started falling apart. He applied that logic to everything, honestly. His favorite armchair had springs literally poking out of the cushion, but he wouldn't let my mom get rid of it. She finally just threw a slipcover over it, one of those stretchy beige ones that never quite fits right and always looks like a wrinkled potato sack... but yeah, people at work have definitely noticed I'm either pacing a lot or moving really slow.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the depressive episode has caused significant impairment, which helps distinguish a major depressive episode (F32.1/F32.9) from adjustment disorder with depressed mood/anxiety (F43.23).
doctor.question: Have these symptoms made it hard for you to function at work or take care of things at home?

target_item.name: Functional Impairment
target_item.manifestation: I’ve had near-missed shifts, mistakes with mortgage paperwork, and more trouble keeping up with POS reports and inventory, which makes me worry I could lose my job and then the condo. I’ve also pulled back from my brother and coworkers enough that people have started noticing I’m not myself.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if the symptoms have affected my ability to function at work or take care of things at home, which directly corresponds to the functional impairment item in my profile.

patient.answer:
Yeah, it really has. I’ve had a few near-missed shifts lately, which is bad. And keeping up with the POS reports and the inventory at the end of the night is just... a massive struggle. Speaking of inventory, we had this huge shortage of those little black cocktail straws last week. Marco ordered the wrong box, and the supplier sent us these giant neon boba tea straws instead. Try serving a classic martini with a bright pink boba straw. It looks completely ridiculous. The customers were actually taking pictures of it, probably putting it on Instagram or whatever. I don't really get Instagram. My brother is always on it, though. 

Actually, I've pulled back from my brother a lot lately. Him and my coworkers, honestly. I've distanced myself enough that people have started noticing I’m not really myself. My brother called me three times on Tuesday and I just sat on the couch and watched the phone ring. He set up this custom ringtone for me on his phone once, it's the theme song from the X-Files. We used to watch that show every Friday night when we were kids. He actually bought one of those "I Want to Believe" UFO posters for his garage. His garage is a total disaster area, completely full of rusty car parts because he's trying to restore a '69 Mustang, but he doesn't actually know the first thing about engines. He buys all these vintage manuals off eBay that smell like a wet basement. 

But yeah, I've been ignoring him, and at home, things are slipping too. I’ve been making stupid mistakes with my mortgage paperwork. It just makes me so worried that I could lose my job because of the near

doctor.intent: Determine whether the depressive syndrome is tied to an identifiable stressor closely enough to support adjustment disorder versus a primary major depressive episode
doctor.question: Do you feel your depression would not have happened if you hadn’t taken on the mortgage?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the causal relationship between the mortgage and the depression (whether it's solely a reaction to the stressor). While the mortgage is mentioned as a context for the onset and feelings of guilt, there is no specific item in the symptom profile that directly addresses this causal hypothetical.

patient.answer:
No, I don't think so. I mean, the mortgage is stressful, sure, but I don't think it caused all this. It's just a lot of paperwork. The bank sends these huge envelopes in the mail, the ones with the little plastic windows on the front. I always rip the plastic window out before I put the envelope in the recycling bin because I read an article once that said the sorting machines at the recycling plant can get jammed if there's too much plastic mixed in with the paper. The article was in this magazine I found in the waiting room at the dentist's office. It was like three years old, too. Why do dentists always have the oldest magazines? There was a whole spread in there about how to make the perfect Thanksgiving turkey, and it was the middle of April. My aunt used to make the best turkey, but she stopped hosting Thanksgiving after her dog knocked over the gravy boat onto the antique rug in the dining room. It was a Persian rug, really intricate patterns, lots of deep reds and blues. She spent a fortune getting it professionally cleaned, but you could still see a faint brown stain if you knew where to look. She ended up putting a potted fern over the spot to hide it, but the fern died because it didn't get enough sunlight in that corner. 

But yeah, the depression... it feels like it would have happened anyway, with or without the house stuff.

inference.note: Ruled out F43.23: although symptoms began after a stressor, the patient now denies the depression would not have happened without the mortgage and endorses a sustained major depressive syndrome (>1 year depressed mood/anhedonia, passive death wish, appetite change, psychomotor change, impairment) not best explained as adjustment disorder.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the depressive episode meets criteria for moderate severity by assessing concentration/indecisiveness, which would distinguish F32.1 from F32.9 given the many already-established depressive symptoms.
doctor.question: Have you been having trouble concentrating?

target_item.name: Diminished_Thinking
target_item.manifestation: I’m having trouble keeping numbers straight on the POS and inventory sheets, and I’ll stare at the screen knowing I’ve done this for years but not trusting what I just entered.
target_item.reason: The doctor is directly asking about trouble concentrating, which aligns with the symptom of diminished thinking.

patient.answer:
Yeah, it's been really bad lately. Like, I’m having so much trouble keeping the numbers straight on the POS and the inventory sheets. I’ll just stare at the screen, and I know I’ve done this for years, but I just can't trust what I just entered. It's like the numbers just float around. 

Speaking of numbers, my cousin used to be obsessed with the lottery. He played the exact same numbers every Wednesday and Saturday for like, ten years straight. It was always 4, 15, 23, 38, 42, and the Powerball was always 7. He swore that 7 was his lucky number because he was born on July 7th at 7:00 AM. He even had this weird little routine where he had to buy the ticket from the exact same gas station on the corner of Elm and Maple, and he had to buy it from this one specific cashier named Brenda. Brenda always wore these enormous hoop earrings, the kind that brush against your shoulders when you turn your head. I always wondered if those were heavy, like if they pulled on your earlobes too much. My mom had a pair of heavy earrings once, these big silver teardrop things she bought on a trip to Santa Fe. She wore them to a wedding and by the end of the night, she was complaining that her ears were throbbing. She ended up taking them off and putting them in her purse, but then she couldn't find her keys because they fell to the bottom of the bag, underneath this massive wad of old receipts she refused to throw away. She was a total packrat with receipts. She kept them in shoeboxes in the closet. But yeah, the concentration thing is definitely an issue at work. I just can't focus on the screen.

doctor.intent: Determine severity by assessing psychotic features, which would distinguish a moderate depressive episode from an unspecified depressive episode.
doctor.question: When you feel guilty or useless, do you ever believe things that other people say aren’t true, like that you deserve punishment or that others would be better off if you were gone?

target_item.name: Worthlessness_Guilt
target_item.manifestation: I came in because I keep feeling like I’ve let my family down by taking on this mortgage, like every small mistake at work proves I’m useless and deserve whatever happens to me.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about feelings of guilt, uselessness, and beliefs of deserving punishment, which aligns directly with the symptom of worthlessness and excessive guilt.

patient.answer:
Yeah... that's actually why I came in. I just keep feeling like I’ve completely let my family down by taking on this mortgage. It's just this heavy weight, you know? 

Speaking of the house, though, it has this massive oak tree in the front yard that drops acorns literally everywhere right now. My neighbor, Mr. Henderson, gets so incredibly mad about it because the acorns roll down my driveway and into the street, and he’s terrified they’re going to dent his car. He drives this pristine 1998 Buick LeSabre. It's this pale mint green color. He washes it every single Sunday morning at exactly 8:00 AM, and he always wears these bright yellow rubber gloves to do it. He told me once he buys the gloves in bulk from a restaurant supply store, which is funny because I work in a restaurant and we use the exact same yellow gloves in the dish pit. Our dishwasher, Tommy, goes through a pair a week because he's always snagging them on the broken dish rack in the back. The owner refuses to fix the rack because he says it costs too much, even though it keeps scratching the bottom of the salad plates. We have these really heavy ceramic plates that chip if you even look at them wrong. 

But anyway, yeah, I just... I feel like every small mistake at work, like with the plates or the POS system, it just proves I’m useless. I really do feel like I deserve whatever bad stuff happens to me.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the depressive episode includes psychotic features by clarifying if the guilt/uselessness beliefs are delusional, which separates moderate depression from unspecified depression.
doctor.question: Do you believe, with certainty, that you deserve to be punished for your mistakes?

target_item.name: Delusions
target_item.manifestation: I can’t shake the feeling that the bank and sometimes even my manager are watching for me to mess up, even when people show me it was just a normal paperwork or register error.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the certainty of the patient's beliefs regarding their mistakes, which probes for the presence of delusions (fixed beliefs).

patient.answer:
I mean, yeah, I do feel like I should be punished, but it's more than just a feeling. It's like... I can't shake this certainty that the bank, and sometimes even my manager at the restaurant, are actively watching me, just waiting for me to mess up. Even when people try to show me that it was just a normal paperwork thing with the mortgage, or a regular register error at work, I know they're watching. 

Which is weird because the register we use is so old. It's one of those clunky touchscreen ones where you have to press really hard, and the screen is all scratched up from people tapping it with the end of a pen. Our bartender, Sarah, she always uses this sparkly pink pen with a giant feather on top. It looks ridiculous, honestly. She bought it at this little novelty shop on the boardwalk when she went to the beach last summer. She went with her sister, who just had a baby, and they rented this tiny cottage that supposedly didn't have air conditioning, which sounds miserable to me. I can't stand the heat. My apartment gets so hot in August because the window unit rattles so loudly I can't sleep if I turn it on. I tried fixing it with duct tape once, but the tape just melted off in the sun. Duct tape isn't as magical as people say it is. 

But yeah, the bank and my manager... I just know they're keeping a close eye on me, waiting for me to fail so they can finally punish me for it.

inference.note: Psychotic features are now evident: mood-congruent delusional guilt/persecution ('bank and manager are watching me... waiting to punish me') in the context of a depressive episode. This rules out F32.1 and F32.9 and supports severe depressive episode with psychotic symptoms.

opening_question.intent: Understand the patient's main reason for seeking psychiatric care today
opening_question.question: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes a major depressive episode with pervasive depressed mood, anhedonia, guilt/worthlessness, impaired concentration, appetite disturbance, psychomotor change, passive death wishes, and functional impairment lasting well beyond 2 weeks. In addition, there are mood-congruent psychotic features: a fixed belief that the bank and manager are watching and waiting to punish him despite others saying this is not true, along with certainty that he deserves punishment. There is no evidence of prior manic episodes in the interview. This supports severe depressive episode with psychotic symptoms.
